# Sieglinde (01, engineer) — SPD-046

## Brief
Close the class of git calls that run a program the Bash hook never analyses, under a verb Law 7 allows, for a member (callers with an agent_id; Spud stays unaffected, as in SPD-044).

Where: bin/spud_ledger.py, the git branch of analyse_segment (about line 6390), beside SPD-044's git_line_defines_alias and git_env_defines_alias and the git-config finding. Tests in tests/test_hooks.py beside GitConfigAliasTest (line 2549), red first.

Design, settled by Spud:
1. Command-line config: refuse a member any `-c` or `--config-env` (spaced and `=` forms, case-folded keys) whose key is outside a short allowlist of inert keys, rather than a denylist of program keys. Build the allowlist from git's documentation, not from memory: keys that change output only (for example color.*, core.quotepath, log.date, i18n.*, advice.*, safe.directory), and justify each in a comment. A key that can name a program or turn one on (core.pager, pager.<cmd>, core.editor, sequence.editor, core.sshCommand, core.hooksPath, core.fsmonitor, diff.external, diff.<driver>.command and textconv, filter.<driver>.clean and smudge, credential.helper, gpg.program and gpg.<format>.program, log.showSignature, remote.<name>.uploadpack and receivepack, protocol.ext and protocol.allow, url.<base>.insteadOf, uploadpack.packObjectsHook, core.askPass, and anything else you find) is refused. core.pager and pager.<cmd> are allowed only with an inert value (empty or `cat`), so `-c core.pager=cat` stays silent. The SPD-044 alias and include refusal keeps its reason; the new refusal gets its own finding and reason naming the key and Law 7.
2. Environment: refuse a member's git call when a variable that names a program is in force on the line (prefix assignment, export, env, as git_env_defines_alias reads GIT_CONFIG_*): GIT_PAGER, PAGER, GIT_EDITOR, VISUAL, EDITOR, GIT_SEQUENCE_EDITOR, GIT_SSH, GIT_SSH_COMMAND, GIT_EXTERNAL_DIFF, GIT_ASKPASS, SSH_ASKPASS, GIT_PROXY_COMMAND, GIT_EXEC_PATH, GIT_TEMPLATE_DIR, and any other git's documentation names. The pager variables with an inert value (empty or `cat`) stay silent, so `GIT_PAGER=cat git log` is allowed.
3. Verb options that name a program under a verb git_refused allows: check its table and cover each allowed verb that takes one (for example `ls-remote` and `fetch` --upload-pack, `grep -O` / --open-files-in-pager, `difftool` -x / --extcmd, `archive --exec`, `submodule foreach`, `bisect run`). A verb already refused needs nothing.

Evidence first: probe read-only from the scratchpad that git honours the forms you test (a pager or ssh command that writes a marker file in the scratchpad is enough; never a real write to the repository or a remote). Record in `member log` which forms you probed.

Proof: red-first tests, then green; a differential over the pre-change hook on a broad corpus of command strings (as Atlantic did at SPD-044) listing every string whose verdict changed, each one intended; the full suite passing (`python3.14 -I -S -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests`). Report the new suite count.

Out of scope, file a proposal if you find more: aliases in on-disk config files (SPD-047), parameter-expansion command words (SPD-043).

Round 2, added by Spud at review (the first return left these open; each probed by Spud from the scratchpad, git 2.50.1, marker written):
4. Abbreviated long options: git's parse-options accepts any unambiguous prefix, so `git ls-remote --upload="<cmd> #" .` ran the command. Match every prefix of each program option that git would accept (--upload-pack, --open-files-in-pager, --extcmd, --exec), with or without `=value`, on each verb in GIT_VERB_PROGRAM_OPTIONS.
5. Clustered short options: `git grep -nO"<cmd>" hi` ran the command. A short-option cluster (`-nO`, `-yx`) that contains the program letter is refused, value attached or not; a false refusal of a pattern value is acceptable, the hook fails closed.
6. The global option `--exec-path=<dir>`: `git --exec-path=<dir> ls-remote https://example.invalid/x` ran `<dir>/git-remote-https`. Refuse it as the command-line form of GIT_EXEC_PATH; bare `--exec-path` (prints the path) stays silent.
7. GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL: enables the ext:: transport, whose URL is a command (`ext::<cmd>`). The harness refused Spud's probe as config injection, which is evidence enough. Add it to the environment list, and read git's environment documentation for any other variable that enables or names a program.
Rerun the red-first tests, the differential and the full suite, then `member result` again with the new count.

## Ticket proposals
- **Bash hook: program-naming options on other allowed git verbs (send-email --sendmail-cmd, instaweb --httpd, web--browse, help viewer)** — suggested P3; created as [[SPD-051]] at P3 by Spud.
  Why: SPD-046 covers program-naming options on ls-remote/fetch (--upload-pack), grep (-O/--open-files-in-pager), difftool (-x/--extcmd) and archive (--exec), the five verbs the brief enumerated and I probed. The same class exists on a few other verbs Law 7 allows: git send-email --sendmail-cmd=<cmd> / --smtp-server=<cmd path> / --to-cmd / --cc-cmd run a program; git instaweb --httpd=<cmd> and instaweb.httpd start one; git web--browse and git help via man.<viewer>.cmd / GIT_MAN_VIEWER run a viewer. The config forms are already refused by SPD-046's allowlist (sendemail.*, instaweb.*, man.* are non-allowlisted keys), so only the command-line OPTION forms of these verbs are uncovered. They are niche (send-email and instaweb are optional git subcommands often not installed), which is why I left them out rather than adding unprobed option names against the brief's evidence-first rule.
  Evidence: GIT_VERB_PROGRAM_OPTIONS in bin/spud_ledger.py lists only ls-remote/fetch/grep/difftool/archive. git help --config shows sendemail.*, instaweb.httpd, man.<tool>.cmd as program keys (refused by the config allowlist); the matching CLI options are not in the table. Not probed here (would need git-email/instaweb installed). Also two minor edges in the same code: a clustered short option like grep -nO is not caught (only -O and -O<pager> are), and a glob expanding to one of the new verbs/options is not in GLOB_SAMPLES.

## Result
SPD-046 rounds 1 and 2 in bin/spud_ledger.py and tests/test_hooks.py, worktree spd-046-git-config-program, uncommitted. A member call to git is now refused under Law 7 whenever it runs or enables a program the hook never analyses, under a verb Law 7 allows. Four vectors closed. First, a -c or --config-env key outside a short inert allowlist of color/advice/i18n/column sections and core.quotepath, core.abbrev, log.date, safe.directory keys, with core.pager and pager.NAME allowed only for an empty or cat value and only in the -c form the hook can read. Second, a program-naming or transport-enabling environment variable in force on the line by prefix, export or env: GIT_EDITOR, GIT_SEQUENCE_EDITOR, EDITOR, VISUAL, GIT_SSH, GIT_SSH_COMMAND, GIT_EXTERNAL_DIFF, GIT_ASKPASS, SSH_ASKPASS, GIT_PROXY_COMMAND, GIT_EXEC_PATH, GIT_TEMPLATE_DIR, GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL, plus GIT_PAGER and PAGER unless empty or cat. Third, a program-naming option on an allowed verb -- ls-remote and fetch --upload-pack, grep -O and --open-files-in-pager, difftool -x and --extcmd, archive --exec -- matched for any unambiguous long prefix such as --upload or --ext with or without an equals value, and any short cluster carrying the program letter such as -nO or -yx, fail-closed. Fourth, the global --exec-path=DIR option and its equals-form abbreviations, the command-line form of GIT_EXEC_PATH, while bare --exec-path stays silent. Each is a new git-program finding with its own Law 7 reason naming the key, variable or option. SPD-044 alias handling and reason are unchanged, and Spud is unaffected. An allowlist was chosen over a denylist because the config docs list about 950 keys with program-naming ones scattered across many sections. VERIFIED by probing git 2.50.1 in a scratch throwaway repo, markers written only in the scratchpad, never a real repo or remote: every round-1 vector plus abbreviated --upload and --open, clustered grep -nO, and --exec-path=DIR ran the program, while bare --exec-path was inert and -c core.pager=cat ran cat. GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL enabling the ext transport is evidenced by the harness refusing the same probe as config injection. New test class GitProgramTest has 15 methods, red-first against HEAD and against my own round-1 code where exactly the four round-2 methods fail and the round-1 methods still pass, green after. Two SPD-044 controls whose keys or vars flipped were updated with cross-references. Differential against HEAD over 2070 command strings: 113 changed verdicts, zero refused-to-silent regressions, each change either newly refused or a reason change on an already-refused command, all git-shaped.
